passage: When the hall clapped and someone shouted "Irfan!", I walked up for the regional sales award holding a trophy that felt heavier than it looked. Looking back, I nearly did what I always used to: smile, say "it was a team effort", and sit down. But that quarter, Pooja had rebuilt our customer list at night, Manoj had driven six hours to close the Nashik order, and Sameera had fixed every invoice error before it reached the client. So I named them, one by one, on stage. On Monday I sent the director an email listing what each of them had done, and split the bonus pool evenly. Pooja later said no leader had ever done that. I didn't do it to be liked. I just knew the trophy had many hands behind it.

qa.q: Who drove six hours to close the Nashik order?
What was Irfan aware of as the trophy felt heavier than it looked?
qa.a: Irfan was aware that the success had many hands behind it, so the credit was not Irfan's alone.

qa.q: What did Irfan do on Monday, and why does it matter?
qa.a: Irfan emailed the director a list of what each person had done and split the bonus pool evenly, so the team's work was seen by senior leaders and shared fairly.

qa.q: What might Pooja have felt when Irfan named the team?
qa.a: Probably valued and trusted, given that Pooja later remarked that no leader had done this before. 😊

grounding: Irfan thanks teammates by name, shares credit and rewards, and tells the director about their contributions.
